Details & sources — rules, caveats, full links

Non-negotiables, whichever day you pick

  • Winter tires are law: BC requires winter tires (M+S or 3-peak snowflake, ≥3.5 mm tread) Oct 1–Apr 30 on Hwy 5 (Coquihalla) and Hwy 1 including Rogers Pass — in effect for this whole trip.
  • Cross passes 10 a.m.–2 p.m. where you can: warmest part of the day, plows have run, full daylight. Never cross either pass at night in this window. (The Mon plan's two crossings — Coquihalla ~3:00–3:30 p.m. on a dry day, Rogers 9:15 a.m. ahead of PM snow — are the deliberate exceptions, chosen because those are each pass's clear windows.)
  • Recheck 48–72 h out: these forecasts were read Sat Oct 24 and will shift — the outlook already moved once that day. Environment Canada reaches Oct 30 and Weather.com Nov 3, so later starts' final legs are outlook only. The DriveBC + ECCC check 2 days before departure is the real decider.

Why Monday works now (the short version)

Sleeping in Revelstoke puts Rogers Pass ~1¼ hrs away, so Tuesday's crossing is ~9:15 a.m. — 5–6 hours before Tuesday's PM snow showers; the ~2.7 cm falls Tuesday night. The earlier objection to Monday assumed a midday Rogers crossing from Kamloops. The one real trade-off is the Kamloops → Revelstoke leg in the dark (~2.5 hrs after a ~5:46 p.m. sunset): darkness/wildlife, not weather — Monday night is cloudy periods, low +3 °C Kamloops / +2 °C Revelstoke, no precipitation forecast. If you'd rather not drive it dark: stay in Kamloops instead — Tuesday's Rogers crossing moves to ~11:30 a.m.–12 p.m. (still ahead of the snow, cushion shrinks to ~2–3 hrs), Day 2 becomes ~620 km, Calgary arrival ~6–6:30 p.m. MDT.

Stays — fine print

The Airbnb basket (C$701 for 7 nights; ≈ C$764 for 8 nights with a second Calgary night; ≈ C$789 with the Regina private-suite version) was verified live on Oct 23, 2026 for the Tue-start dates — re-check prices live before booking any shifted start date; the Mon plan (Revelstoke swapped in for Kamloops) was re-checked on Oct 24, 2026 for Oct 26–Nov 1: all 7 nights dated-verified — Swiss Chalet Motel Revelstoke C$99, Calgary The Cozy Nook C$62.01, Regina PAJO C$74.37, Winnipeg C$95.24, Thunder Bay Kelly's Corner Room #1 C$112.53, Sault C$155.29, Sudbury “Queen size bed & continental breakfast” C$84.80 — budget total C$683.24; C$732.73 with the Calgary (The Cove C$83.25) and Sudbury (The Guest Suite, Hanmer C$113.05) entire-unit upgrades, under the $800 cap. The original Calgary, Thunder Bay and Sudbury picks were unavailable on the shifted dates, so the dated replacements above are the picks. Hotel prices are research proxies except one exact dated night: Regina Meridian, Wed Oct 28–29, 2026 (C$113). The Tue plan's hotels cost more because it puts Thunder Bay on Saturday Oct 31 — Halloween (comparable 8.6–9.0-rated properties at C$197–244 that weekend); the Fri Oct 30 start opens with weekend nights. Cheaper properties in every city were excluded for failing the rating or vibe bar (dated/dingy photos, cleanliness complaints). Cancellation notes: the Calgary Cozy Nook (C$62.01) and the Thunder Bay Richmond Inn alt (C$113) are non-refundable; Kelly's Corner allows free cancellation before Oct 29; both Sudbury picks allow free cancellation for 24 hours; The Cove (Calgary alt) allows free cancellation before 4:00 p.m. Oct 26; refundable-until dates weren't shown for most hotel picks — confirm at booking. Nothing is booked; this is research only.

Ranking & climatology caveat

Ranking: A (Mon Oct 26) recommended; C (Fri Oct 30, both passes bone-dry) and D (Sun Oct 25) close behind; then E1 (Oct 31), E2 (Nov 2), B (Tue Oct 27) last. Later starts carry a climatological risk the early ones don't: Sault Ste. Marie's snowy season starts ~Oct 24–26 and November averages ~10 cm of snow, rising steeply through the month (WeatherSpark). Prairie legs are mostly dry/cloudy in every scenario (watch Regina wind — gusts to 77 km/h on Oct 24).
